His wife was left with the debts and no insurance; the loaf and the flour never passed through her hands.

Paris 20th arrondissement, Belleville — bakery
Poisoning
Apprentice

The kraft bag Garnier brought:
· A gluten-free flour blend (rice, buckwheat) containing finely ground dried monkshood root: aconitine.
· The powder is not uniform; the root powder is concentrated in the top of the bag. The mixture was added after the bag was filled.
· Fingerprints on the outside of the bag: Rayan Haddad (expected) and Sophie Garnier.
FLOUR BAG ANALYSIS
Catering coordinator.
Client information is confidential.
A gentleman from the auction house brought it; he said, ‘Mr Delorme’s own trusted flour, his allergy is very severe.’ I only carried it. I didn’t even open the packet.
She holds the strap of her bag with both hands.
Where did you get the flour?
Sophie Garnier — interview
On the records.
Sophie Garnier — second interview
No.
Of course my prints will be on it, I carried it. The gentleman who brought it…

Five thousand euros. The firm was going under. The man said, ‘Delorme is old, his heart is weak anyway, no one will ask.’ He gave me the powder himself; I mixed it into the bag, in the van. I didn’t know the baker would taste it; if I’d known… I didn’t ask his name. He said he was from the auction house’s shipping department, gave no business card; tall, a ring on his left hand.
You added the root powder to the bag.
Monkshood root (aconitine) mixed into the gluten-free flour
Something was put in his coffee
A spontaneous heart rhythm disorder
How?
The victim’s wife.
The bakery’s accounts are my business.
Didier? He gave credit to half the neighbourhood. We have debts, yes, we have no insurance, yes; his death has left me nothing but debt. No one would want to kill Didier.
She knots and unknots her apron string.
Did Didier have enemies?
Ms Garnier’s firm. An auction house dinner; bread for a hundred people, plus a single gluten-free loaf. It’s written on the order form.
What was that special order?
Nadine Fontaine — interview
BREAD  /  POISONING
In Belleville, a baker dies at four in the morning, poisoned by a loaf he tasted. Everyone in the neighbourhood loved him.
FILE #033

Form sent to the bakery by the catering firm, 15 May:

· 120 small country loaves — Maison Delorme, post-auction dinner, 16 May.
· 1 gluten-free loaf, to be packed SEPARATELY — ‘Table 1: M. Auguste Delorme (coeliac). Flour to be supplied by the client.’

Signed by: Sophie Garnier, coordinator.
ORDER FORM
41, coordinator at a catering firm; places special orders with the bakery.
Sophie Garnier
55, the bakery’s co-owner; the victim’s wife.
Nadine Fontaine
22, the bakery’s apprentice; he prepares the dough on the night shift.
Rayan Haddad
Apprentice.
My master taught me, I do it.

It isn’t ours. The lady from the catering firm brought it at five in the morning and handed it to me at the door: ‘The client’s own flour, severe allergy, don’t use any other flour.’ I made the dough with that flour, my master put it in the oven.
Where did you get the gluten-free flour?
The flour? …I opened that bag. Nothing happened to my hands, I wear gloves. The lady gave it to me at five, I kneaded it. Don’t look at me as if it were my fault.
“It goes in my mouth before it goes in the customer’s.”
He tastes every special loaf. Forty years’ habit. ‘It goes in my mouth before it goes in the customer’s,’ he used to say. Gluten-free ones burn easily, so he cut that loaf first.
He squeezes his cap in both hands.
Why did the master taste that loaf?
Rayan Haddad — interview

On 16 May 2030 at 04.25, in a bakery in Belleville, baker Didier Fontaine (58) collapsed beside the counter. The apprentice Rayan Haddad made an emergency call; Didier died on the way.

On the counter, a small gluten-free loaf with one slice cut and bitten. Before death: vomiting, numbness in the arms, an irregular pulse.

Overnight the bakery was preparing special orders: a catering firm’s 11.00 delivery.
INCIDENT REPORT
Send the flour bag for analysis
Request the order form
Request permission to search the catering van

Toxicology found the poison in the loaf; the order form showed who the loaf was going to, the camera who brought the bag, and the analysis that the powder was added afterwards. The van search, opened on two grounds, gave the cash, the second bag and the messages.
The person who died may not be the target. First ask who the poison was going to, then whose hands it passed through on the way.
Belleville — May 2030

After Mercier’s arrest, someone afraid that the auction house’s owner Auguste Delorme would talk gave Sophie Garnier, the indebted catering coordinator, five thousand euros and a pouch of monkshood root powder. Garnier mixed the powder into the bag she brought to the bakery as Delorme’s ‘own gluten-free flour’. Baker Didier Fontaine, in his habit of tasting every special loaf before the client, ate the first slice of that loaf and died.
Who prepared the poison?
FILE #033  /  BUBE PARIS — BELLEVILLE
15 May
File #033 — Bread

· Aconitine (from the monkshood plant) in the blood and stomach contents. It disrupts the heart rhythm; effect within minutes.
· Stomach: only a few mouthfuls of bread and coffee.
· The rest of the loaf: aconitine, high concentration; mixed through the whole dough.
· The bakery’s other doughs and flours: clean.
TOXICOLOGY

The firm’s van used by Sophie Garnier (with the branch chief’s approval):

· In the glovebox, a white envelope holding €5,000 in cash.
· In the door pocket, another folded kraft bag of the same type, empty; aconitine powder at the bottom.
· On her phone, 14 May, a message from an unregistered number: ‘The bag tomorrow morning. Table 1 only. The rest clean.’
· From the same number, 12 May: ‘After Mercier, Delorme will talk. Before he does.’
